name: Eliphaz
title: Job's friend from Teman
summary: Eliphaz the Temanite was the first and most prominent of Job's three friends who came to comfort him in his suffering. He represented traditional wisdom theology and claimed that Job's sufferings must be the result of sin. In the end, he was rebuked by God for not speaking rightly about Him and had to offer a burnt offering while Job prayed for him.

keyEvents.title: Eliphaz comes to comfort Job
keyEvents.description: Eliphaz the Temanite, along with Bildad and Zophar, traveled to Job when they heard about his misfortune. They sat silently with him for seven days and seven nights before beginning to speak.

keyEvents.title: Eliphaz's first speech
keyEvents.description: Eliphaz delivered his first speech to Job, arguing that the innocent do not perish and suggesting that Job's suffering must be due to sin. He also recounted a night vision he had experienced.

keyEvents.title: Eliphaz's second speech
keyEvents.description: In his second speech, Eliphaz became more direct in his accusations against Job, claiming that Job's own words proved his guilt. He alleged that Job despised reverence for God and rejected humility.

keyEvents.title: Eliphaz's Third Speech with Direct Accusations
keyEvents.description: In his third and final speech, Eliphaz directly accused Job of specific sins, such as taking pledges from his brothers without cause, refusing water to the thirsty, and food to the hungry. He urged Job to return to God.

keyEvents.title: God Rebukes Eliphaz
keyEvents.description: After God spoke to Job from the storm, He turned to Eliphaz and said that His wrath was kindled against him and his two friends because they had not spoken rightly about God as Job had done.

keyEvents.title: Eliphaz Offers Sacrifices and Job Prays for Him
keyEvents.description: God commanded Eliphaz and his friends to offer seven bulls and seven rams as a burnt offering, and that Job should pray for them. When Job prayed for his friends, the Lord forgave them and restored Job's fortunes.
